key_insight: Random train/test splits overestimate perovskite ML performance because many records are duplicated recipes, so grouped splits are needed to measure true generalisation.
engineering_relevance: For device optimization, this protocol helps engineers choose models and claims that remain reliable on new materials, new papers, and new institutions rather than just memorized historical recipes.
method: Mapped institutional provenance in the Perovskite Database
Built a hierarchy of grouped splits isolating duplicates, publications, and institutions
Benchmarked 13 models and compared rankings across split types
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that nearly two-thirds of curated devices share an exact recipe with another, and model rankings shift sharply from random splits to unseen-institution and future-discovery splits.
watch_item: Grouped evaluation may reduce apparent accuracy, so model selection and benchmarking must be aligned with the intended deployment setting.
paper_title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics
